relationships.claim: Hepatocytes across the hepatic acinus have spatially heterogeneous metabolic capacities; periportal and perivenous zones differ in multiple metabolic functions, and this zonation is dynamic rather than a fixed uniform property of the liver.
Glucose and fatty-acid metabolic pathways are zonated across the liver acinus, and perturbation of this spatial organization has been described in the context of metabolic liver disease.

The reviewed adult hepatic acinus shows zonation of metabolic functions, including predominance of xenobiotic metabolism in the perivenous region; this is an educational physiology/pharmacology relationship and not a basis for drug selection or dosing.
